findings.title: create ignores alias_level
findings.body: The client's asJSON sends alias_level, and update applies it, but create only sets name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level silently gets the default instead.

findings.title: totalPages off by one when count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, so 50 users with limit 50 gives 2 pages. The Next button stays enabled and leads to an empty page. It should use Math.ceil(user_count/limit).

findings.title: Unbounded limit on public members endpoint
findings.body: The limit parameter is user-controlled with no cap. A request such as limit=1000000 on a large automatic group serializes every user, which is a cheap DoS vector. Clamp it to a sane maximum, and also guard against negative or zero values.

findings.title: Breaking change to members.json response format
findings.body: /groups/:id/members.json used to return an array and now returns an object with members and meta keys. Any other consumers that expect the old array shape will break, such as the user-selector, plugins, or API clients.

findings.title: automatic not in scope of item view
findings.body: Inside the each itemView, the template's context is the view, not the group. The `automatic` binding there likely does not resolve to the group's automatic flag, so the remove link may be shown for automatic groups. Clicking it would only produce a 422 error.

findings.title: remove_member automatic test uses wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes without exercising the real route.

findings.title: addMembers errors unhandled and input not cleared
findings.body: addMembers has no error handler, so a 422 response (for example on an automatic group) fails silently. The usernames field is also never reset after adding, as the TODO in the code notes.
